episode_title: Key Takeaways from the Fiscal Year 2027 Hospice Final Rule

real_qa.q: What is the Service and Spending Variation Index (SSVI) in the Fiscal Year 2027 Hospice Final Rule and what SSVI score triggers CMS review?
real_qa.r: The SSVI is a scoring system built from nine claims-based metrics covering live discharge rates, length of stay over 180 days, skilled nursing minutes, weekend visit rates, and total non-hospice spending. CMS indicated that a score of 13 or higher would be roughly the 99th percentile and would flag a hospice as an outlier worth further review, whether that's medical review, education, or in serious cases, payment suspension or revocation.
real_qa.requete: SSVI score CMS hospice review threshold

real_qa.q: What did CMS identify about carrier claims for pressure ulcers and skin substitutes in the Fiscal Year 2027 Hospice Final Rule?
real_qa.r: In the final rule, skin substitutes and wound care came up repeatedly, and CMS noted that carrier claims for pressure ulcers increased almost 4,000% from fiscal year 2020 to fiscal year 2024. CMS pushed back hard on the idea that this is purely a non-hospice provider problem outside of hospice control.
real_qa.requete: CMS pressure ulcers claims increase 4000 percent 2020 2024

real_qa.q: What changes did CMS make to the Election Statement Addendum requirements effective October 1, 2026?
real_qa.r: Before October 1, 2026, the addendum provision was conditioned on the patient requesting it and the hospice determining the patient had something unrelated to hospice. On October 1, 2026, those conditions collapsed, and the addendum is now required to be provided to every Medicare beneficiary at hospice admission within five days of admission. The addendum does not have to be signed within five days; it only needs to be furnished within that timeframe.
real_qa.requete: Election Statement Addendum October 1 2026 Medicare hospice

real_qa.q: What is CMS asking about medical aid in dying (MAID) in the Fiscal Year 2027 Hospice Final Rule and what is CMS's current position?
real_qa.r: CMS asked hospices how they handle patients who pursue MAID and whether they continue providing hospice care, encourage revocation, and what happens to unused medication. In the final rule, CMS clarified that this RFI does not signal a coming proposal to integrate MAID into the hospice benefit and that it is purely fact-finding to understand whether additional oversight is needed to keep federal funds walled off for MAID-related items and services, as federal law flatly prohibits using Medicare funds for anything related to causing a patient's death.
real_qa.requete: CMS medical aid dying MAID Medicare hospice policy 2027

real_qa.q: What palliative care expansion topics did CMS request input on in the Fiscal Year 2027 Hospice Final Rule?
real_qa.r: CMS asked for input on community-based palliative care outside of hospice, requesting information on how providers currently bill for palliative services under Part B evaluation and management codes, advanced care planning codes, and chronic care management codes, and where gaps exist. Commenters broadly supported expanding community palliative care and floated ideas like a dedicated palliative care assessment code, bundled or capitated palliative care benefit, new billing codes for social workers and community health workers, and making palliative care telehealth flexibilities permanent.
real_qa.requete: CMS palliative care expansion benefit codes 2027 final rule
